title: Associate Legal Counsel, Real Estate and Project Development
description:
Silicon Ranch is a fully integrated provider of customized renewable energy, carbon, and battery storage solutions for a diverse set of partners across North America.

  • We are known for putting community partnerships first, and are the only renewable energy company in the U.S. that owns and operates all of its solar ranches and has a 100% track record for successful delivery.

  • We have the largest utility scale agrivoltaics portfolio in the country under Regenerative Energy®, our nationally recognized holistic approach to project design, construction, and land management. Our model incorporates regenerative ranching and other regenerative land management practices to restore livelihoods and soil health, biodiversity, and water quality.

  • Through our subsidiary, Clearloop, we are able to help businesses of all sizes reclaim their carbon footprint with a direct investment in building new solar projects while also helping bring renewable energy and economic development to distressed communities.

By joining Silicon Ranch, you will be joining a team of experienced and dedicated individuals who have proven time and again that it is indeed possible to not only “make solar do more”, but to make the promise of carbon-free, renewable energy that benefits people right where it comes from a tangible, measurable, and replicable reality.

Silicon Ranch is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace that is reflective of the communities in which we work and serve. We are an equal opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.

Job Description

Position: Associate Legal Counsel, Real Estate and Project Development

Location: Nashville, TN (remote considered on a case by case basis)

Silicon Ranch Legal Department Mission Statement: The Silicon Ranch Legal Department, leveraging years of legal practice and a deep and holistic understanding of Silicon Ranch’s business and structure, is committed to providing support to all business units by providing law firm quality, company-tailored legal services and counsel in an efficient, reliable, practical, professional, comprehensible, and approachable manner, thus enabling our internal stakeholders to:

  • Execute their commercial and operational objectives in a risk-appropriate fashion;
  • Employ sound decision-making in all facets of company operations;
  • Comply with applicable laws, regulations, internal policies, and best practices; and
  • Appropriately reduce exposure to formal disputes, reputational harm, and associated costs through the effective identification, mitigation, and allocation of legal and commercial risks.

Role Overview: We are seeking a commercial real estate attorney (4-7+ years’ experience) to support legal aspects of the Company’s project development, external affairs and real estate business functions. This role partners closely with the Senior Legal Counsel, Real Estate & Project Development and Legal Counsel, Real Estate & Project Development, and several cross-functional business teams within the Company to negotiate, diligence, and de-risk the real estate operations of the Company. As such, the ideal candidate is proactive and demonstrates subject matter mastery of title, survey and real estate purchase and sale transactions. The right candidate can independently identifying risk and effectively communicate sound legal advice that is tailored to the practical needs of the Company.

Core Responsibilities: As Associate Legal Counsel, Real Estate & Project Development, the candidate will support the real estate, project development and external affairs functions of the Company, including a combination of the following:

  • Site Control Transactions: Independently manage the negotiation and administration of purchase options, easement agreements, and their subsequent closing transactions. This includes title and survey diligence and de-risking; closing document drafting and negotiation; and independently managing transaction logistics.
  • Project Finance Support: Draft, negotiate, and administer key real estate agreements and title and survey deliverables for project financing transactions. This includes easements, affiliate ground leases, and complex title and survey requirements.
  • Land Use Permitting Support: Advise and support the Company’s External Affairs and Project Development teams on local land use permitting and zoning ordinance review and strategy.
  • Outside Counsel Management: Efficiently supervise outside counsels where engaged, though expect that much of the legal work will be managed in-house by the candidate.
  • General Diligence Support: Serve as a trusted legal advisor to the Project Development, External Affairs, and Project Finance teams and provide legal support on broader real estate-related topics as needed in support of the growth of the Company. This may include regulatory, environmental or corporate governance matters.

Execution Expectations: As Associate Legal Counsel, Real Estate & Project Development, the candidate will:

  • Manage multiple transactions and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Effectively identify business risks facing the Company.
  • Deliver practical, balanced legal advice to the Company’s business units.
  • Communicate clearly and effectively, both in writing and orally, with internal and external stakeholders of mixed levels of sophistication.
  • Represent the organization professionally with landowners, local officials, financing partners, and other project stakeholders.

Education: J.D. degree from an ABA-accredited US law school; active bar admission in good standing in at least one state.

Experience:

  • Minimum of 4 years of experience as a real estate attorney at a top-tier law firm or in-house legal department.
  • Substantial experience with real estate purchase and sale transactions, title and survey review, including experience leading transactions and diligence independently. This position has an emphasis on the fundamentals of real estate and property law, executed at a high level of complexity.
  • Significant emphasis is placed on mastery of the basic tenets of real estate and property law, but executed at a high level of complexity. Renewable energy experience preferred but not required.
  • Demonstrated ability to:
  • Manage multiple priorities concurrently with strong attention to detail and organization.
  • Provide pragmatic, business-oriented advice.
  • Build relationships with internal stakeholders.
  • If remote, maintain strong relationships and collaboration with both remote colleagues and in-office teams.

Our interview process:

A typical interview process at Silicon Ranch might include the below stages. Please note that we may make changes to these steps as needed, and details will be provided to you early on in the process.

  1. Introductory Interview with our recruiter
  2. Hiring Manager Interview to dive into technical skills and behavioral questions
  3. Panel Interview to assess cross-functional skills and dive deeper into technical skills
  4. Executive Interview to answer high-level questions about SRC and the team

Job Description

Position: Associate, Project Development

Location: Nashville, TN

Overview: This position will provide development and pre-construction support activities. This will require coordination with the Business Development, Interconnection, Public Affairs, and EPC teams to facilitate project needs, including site selection (as necessary to support real estate team), site due diligence, site acquisition, entitlements, environmental permitting, site assessments, budget development and management, scheduling etc. This work may require some periods of travel, generally 4-7 days per month. This position will support permitting, consulting services, engineering, reporting and the general project management required for successful project development and pre-construction support.

Main Responsibilities:

  • Lead project site due diligence activities, including title and mineral title review, permitting research, land development assessments, and identification of planning and zoning challenges.
  • Manage the full site development lifecycle by assessing, mitigating, and monitoring project risks while ensuring development milestones are achieved on schedule.
  • Partner with Interconnection, Business Development, Development Engineering, and Delivery teams to develop accurate project schedules and identify early-stage site risks.
  • Develop and manage project development budgets, oversee consultant and vendor activities, and ensure all work is completed on time and within budget.
  • Coordinate and oversee project development activities, including land research, environmental assessments, preliminary site design, permitting, surveys, geotechnical investigations, and pre-construction planning.
  • Support project permitting efforts and represent projects during public hearings while building productive relationships with landowners, clients, utilities, government agencies, consultants, contractors, and other stakeholders.
  • Assist with project contracting, design coordination, and the communication of project risks, site constraints, and development requirements to Delivery and EPC teams.
  • Collaborate across multidisciplinary teams to identify client and vendor challenges, develop creative solutions, and ensure successful project advancement from site selection through pre-construction.

Qualifications:

Education:

Bachelor's Degree, preferably in Energy/Land Management, Environmental Studies, or equivalent; additional educational qualifications such as a PMP or MBA considered.

Experience:

0 - 2 years of work experience in project management, land development or real estate.

Technical:

Exposure or experience to the US energy and/or renewable market desirable.

Job Description

Position: Construction Oversight Manager

Location: Field-based position (Tennessee Valley area preferred)

Overview: The Construction Oversight Manager is a fully field-based position responsible for overseeing the successful execution of solar energy projects from inception to completion. This role requires working on-site at project locations throughout the Tennessee Valley region to directly supervise construction activities, manage teams, ensure compliance with safety regulations, and maintain high-quality standards. The Construction Oversight Manager works closely with project stakeholders, subcontractors, and company management to ensure projects are completed on time, within budget, and with a focus on safety and quality.

Main Responsibilities:

On-site Project Oversight:

  • Serve as the primary on-site representative for all construction-related activities.
  • Collaborate with project engineers, designers, and stakeholders to develop construction plans and schedules.
  • Create detailed project timelines, outlining milestones, tasks, and resource allocation.
  • Monitor and adjust project schedules as needed to ensure timely project completion.

Team Management:

  • Supervise on-site construction teams, including subcontractors and company personnel.
  • Assign tasks, delegate responsibilities, and provide clear instructions to team members.
  • Foster a collaborative and productive work environment, encouraging teamwork and effective communication.

Safety and Compliance:

  • Ensure that all construction activities comply with safety regulations, codes, and company policies.
  • Conduct regular safety meetings and inspections to identify potential hazards and implement corrective actions.
  • Monitor the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and adherence to safety protocols.

Quality Control:

  • Monitor construction progress to ensure work is executed according to design specifications and industry standards.
  • Conduct regular quality checks and inspections through the contractor’s QC inspectors to identify and address any deviations from project requirements.
  • Report non-conformance and deficiencies through ProCore and elevating concerns as needed.

Resource Management:

  • Coordinate the procurement and allocation of construction materials, equipment, and tools.
  • Optimize resource utilization to minimize project costs while maintaining quality and safety standards.

Communication and Reporting:

  • Provide weekly QA/QC updates to project stakeholders, including company management and clients, on project progress and any potential issues.
  • Document project activities, changes, and challenges in detailed reports.

Problem Solving:

  • Identify and address construction-related challenges and issues promptly to prevent delays and maintain project momentum.
  • Collaborate with relevant teams to develop solutions and implement corrective actions.

Budget Management:

  • Monitor project expenses and ensure adherence to the allocated budget.
  • Identify cost-saving opportunities and propose changes to project plans when necessary.

Qualifications:

  • Mandatory Field Presence: Ability and willingness to work 100% on-site at construction project locations across the Tennessee Valley region.
  • Bachelor's degree in construction management, engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • Minimum of 5 years’ experience in managing construction projects, preferably in the renewable energy or solar industry.
  • Current OSHA 30; First Aid/CPR; and USACE Construction Quality Control Management certifications; or ability to obtain within 30 days of hire.
  • Strong knowledge of construction techniques, safety protocols, and quality standards.
  • Excellent leadership, organizational and communication skills to effectively manage teams and collaborate with stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in project management software and tools (Microsoft Office & Procore). Familiar with USACE RMS CM and EM-385-1-1
  • Problem-solving abilities and a proactive approach to addressing challenges.
  • Attention to detail and a commitment to ensuring high-quality work.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing project requirements.

Job Description

Position: Contracts Manager

Location: Remote

Overview: Silicon Ranch develops, builds, owns, and operates utility-scale solar energy projects, and the agreements behind those projects are how our work gets done. As Contract Manager, you are the commercial owner of the contracts that bring our projects to life. This includes EPC and construction services agreements, consulting agreements, and professional services agreements. You will lead sourcing and negotiation, manage supplier relationships and performance, and identify and mitigate commercial risk, all in close partnership with our Legal, Engineering, Finance, and Delivery teams.


This is a hands-on commercial role for someone who enjoys both the deal and the disciplined follow-through that makes a contract perform.

Main Responsibilities:

Sourcing & RFP process

  • Lead the RFI/RFP process end to end: build bid/solicitation packages with engineering, finance, project management, and development, and ensure complete, accurate bid documents.
  • Facilitate pre-bid meetings and manage communication with bidders throughout the solicitation.
  • Drive competitive sourcing that delivers cost savings and maximizes the value of spend.

Bid evaluation & award

  • Coordinate cross-functional bid evaluation and lead bid analysis across price, schedule, scope, and commercial risk.
  • Coordinate and lead internal and external bid review meetings and present award recommendations to leadership.

Negotiation & contracting

  • Serve as the external communicator in negotiations with contractors and suppliers, leading negotiations and making commercial recommendations.
  • Identify and mitigate commercial and contractual risks.
  • Draft, redline, and negotiate commercial terms and conditions partnering with Legal and other departments.
  • Maintain a library of standard templates, fallback positions, and a negotiation playbook in coordination with Legal.
  • Coordinate contract execution: signature routing, execution, and distribution of fully executed agreements.

Supplier & risk management

  • Identify, prequalify, and onboard new vendors; maintain qualification and approved-supplier status.
  • Manage EPC/supplier performance through scorecards and periodic business reviews.
  • Identify and mitigate commercial and contractual risk across the lifecycle

Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of contract management, commercial, or procurement experience, including at least 2 years working directly with EPC or construction contracts.
  • Experience in utility-scale renewable energy, power, infrastructure, heavy civil, or large construction/EPC; utility-scale solar or renewables preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience leading commercial negotiations of high-value EPC, construction, or supply agreements.
  • Hands-on experience drafting, redlining, and administering commercial agreements, with working command of key commercial terms (payment/milestones, LDs, warranties, indemnification, limitation of liability, insurance, change orders, termination).
  • Familiarity with EPC/construction services agreement structures.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration with delivery, engineering, finance, development, and legal teams.
  • Bachelor’s degree in construction management, business, finance, supply chain, engineering, economics, or a related field or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Preferred: relevant certification (NCMA CPCM/CFCM, ISM CPSM, or PMP).

Job Description

Position: Interconnection Project Manager

Location: Remote

Overview:

The Interconnection Project Manager supports the day-to-day execution of Silicon Ranch's interconnection process for an assigned portfolio of development and acquired projects. This role requires close coordination with multi-disciplinary internal teams, the ability to identify and understand utility and internal client issues, and the ability to work collaboratively to develop and communicate creative solutions in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. The position necessitates interaction with clients including utilities, financial institutions, off-takers, investors, government agencies, consultants, and other organizations.

SRC's Interconnection Project Manager is responsible for managing the interconnection process for assigned projects across the company's target markets. This position is critical to executing the company's development initiatives and supports market analyses and transmission-related topics, including but not limited to utility tariffs, planning processes, and the overall interconnection process. The position also works closely with internal staff, consultants, and other subject matter experts as needed to execute the company's interconnection and development strategy.

Main Responsibilities:

Management of the Interconnection Process

  • Manage the interconnection process and negotiations for assigned development and acquired projects, from siting to execution, including interconnection agreements, system studies, affected systems studies, and engineering agreements
  • Coordinate required power flow simulation analysis, models, and congestion studies (internally or externally) to support siting, IA, PPA, financing, and origination processes
  • Track and manage interconnection commercial arrangements to support optimization for cost, schedule, and risk
  • Build and maintain productive working relationships with utilities, ISOs, and industry representatives on assigned projects
  • Serve as the primary point of contact on interconnection status and risk for assigned projects, escalating issues to the VP of Interconnection as needed
  • Support the regional interconnection team's processes and best practices
  • Support due diligence review of potential project and portfolio acquisitions related to interconnection and transmission risk, and provide input to the acquisition team

New and Existing Market Planning and Analysis:

  • Support the development and execution of tactical plans for new and existing markets, working with the Regional Interconnection Managers, Project Development, and Origination
  • Track tariff, planning, accessibility, and interconnection process developments for new and existing markets and flag changes to leadership
  • Coordinate with internal resources and consultants as necessary to implement SRC's goals

Project Development/Project Delivery:

  • Provide input to Project Development and Project Delivery on utility system loading, deliverability, congestion, and potential interconnection costs for the siting of new development projects, in conjunction with Regional Interconnection Managers and Utility Planning
  • Support evaluation of interconnection and gen-tie alternatives to optimize project interconnection options based on cost, schedule, off-take preference, and risk
  • Support project ranking and prioritization based on transmission capacity, queue position, and interconnection cost/risk profile
  • Provide interconnection cost and timeline input to support budget forecasting and project underwriting at key development-stage gates
  • Support Project Delivery during construction by tracking interconnection agreement milestones, utility-required studies, and equipment/testing coordination to keep projects on schedule for commercial operation
  • Coordinate with Project Delivery and utilities on interconnection facility construction, witness testing, and energization to support timely achievement of commercial operation

Qualifications:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Project Management, or a related field preferred, with a desired emphasis on power

Experience:

  • 2-4 years' experience in power generation interconnections; solar and project siting experience strongly preferred
  • Experience with WECC interconnection processes is a plus
  • Working knowledge of generation interconnection tariffs, interconnection agreements, and requirements in one or more key markets, including familiarity with the process from initial interconnection request through utility operations
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong project management, communication, and negotiation skills

Technical:

  • Relevant experience in the US renewable energy market, project development, or interconnection experience is desirable
  • Familiarity with grid operations topics
  • Working knowledge of the transmission system planning process
  • Working knowledge of interconnection agreements and ability to support negotiation of utility acceptance of SRC modifications
  • General knowledge of power flow modeling and results
  • Ability to establish strong working relationships with utilities, ISOs, and industry representatives
  • Strong public speaking and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical topics and write technical reports
  • Strong collaboration and problem-solving skills, capable of applying engineering principles to identify and solve issues
  • High-energy, positive attitude with the ability to receive constructive feedback

Job Description

Position: Senior Manager, Sourcing

Location: Remote

Overview:

Silicon Ranch develops, builds, owns, and operates utility-scale solar and renewable energy projects across the U.S. The Senior Manager, Supply Chain owns the strategy, sourcing, and risk posture for the major equipment that powers our projects, which includes modules, transformers, inverters, racking, and other major equipment. You will set multi-year category and sourcing strategy, be responsible for the equipment budget and savings targets, lead and develop members of the supply chain team, and serve as a senior point of accountability for supply continuity, cost, and trade compliance.

You will collaborate closely with engineering, legal, contract management, project management, project finance, and operations, and partner with Legal on legal terms without serving as legal counsel.

Main Responsibilities:

Strategy, category & vendor management

  • Help set and execute multi-year procurement and category strategy for key equipment (modules, transformers, inverters, racking, and other major equipment).
  • Build and maintain long-term strategic supplier relationships that ensure cost competitiveness, quality, and reliability of supply.
  • Lead supplier selection, negotiation, and contract execution to secure optimal commercial terms.
  • Run Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and supplier performance metrics/scorecards to drive accountability and continuous improvement.

Commercial & contract management

  • Structure and negotiate Master Supply Agreements (MSAs) and long-term, portfolio-scale procurement frameworks.
  • Contribute to domestic content strategy in coordination with project finance/tax and legal to support investment tax credits and secure and maintain compliance certifications.
  • Responsible for the equipment budget and savings targets.
  • Develop, refine, and govern procurement policies and procedures to improve efficiency, transparency, and communication.

Trade compliance & risk

  • Serve as senior owner of trade compliance for equipment sourcing.
  • Manage commodity risk (steel, copper, aluminum, etc.), advising on forward cost curves and budgetary impacts.
  • Ensure supply continuity through prequalification, supplier financial-health monitoring, allocation management, and contingency planning.

Planning, logistics & execution

  • Ensure effective scheduling, tracking, and delivery of owner furnished equipment to meet construction timelines, including inventory, warehousing, staging, and laydown coordination.
  • Coordinate quality and factory acceptance testing (FAT)/source inspection and non-conformance resolution with Engineering.
  • Integrate procurement schedules and specifications into RFPs and EPC subcontracts, in partnership with the delivery teams.

Leadership & team development

  • Mentor, and develop the supply chain team and build the processes and governance that scale the function.
  • Elevate the team’s commercial and negotiation capability and alignment with procurement best practices.
  • Act as a strategic liaison between procurement and cross-functional teams to drive operational excellence, alignment, and efficiency.

Qualifications:

  • 6-8 years in strategic sourcing, procurement, or supply chain, including demonstrated people-leadership (leading a team and/or developing other managers) and portfolio- or program-scale ownership.
  • Experience in renewables, power, construction, infrastructure, or a related industry; utility-scale solar or renewables strongly preferred.
  • Proven track record negotiating complex commercial transactions and long-term/master agreements, with emphasis on cost control, risk management, and supplier performance.
  • Experience with EPC contracts and logistics coordination for major equipment.
  • Trade-compliance depth relevant to solar: UFLPA/traceability, customs, and domestic content strategy for the ITC.
  • Strong financial acumen for pricing trends, commodity fluctuations, TCO/should-cost, budget ownership, and supply-chain risk.
  • Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Excellent communication skills, able to engage and influence internal and external stakeholders, including senior leadership.
  • Bachelor’s in business, supply chain, finance, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Preferred: MBA, ISM CPSM, or APICS/ASCM CPIM/CSCP.

Job Description

Position: Senior Power Conversion Engineer

Location: Remote

Overview:

The Senior Power Conversion Engineer is responsible for the performance, reliability, and lifecycle management of power conversion systems across the operating fleet, including inverters, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and related AC equipment.


This role serves as the technical owner of power conversion system performance—bridging field execution, engineering analysis, and vendor engagement. The position informs equipment selection and design standards for new projects while driving resolution of both systemic and site-specific issues.

Main Responsibilities:

· Own the performance and availability of inverter and BESS systems across the fleet.

· Drive the resolution of major failures, sustained underperformance, and serial defects.

· Track and analyze performance and reliability metrics to identify emerging risks.

· Provide advanced troubleshooting support for complex inverter, BESS, and AC system issues.

· Translate field observations into clear problem statements and actionable solutions.

· Support O&M teams with structured troubleshooting and escalation.

· Serve as the primary engineering interface with inverter and BESS OEMs and service providers.

· Lead technical escalation and resolution of systemic equipment issues, including root cause identification and corrective action implementation.

· Provide technical oversight of vendor performance, ensuring equipment issues are properly diagnosed, addressed, and resolved.

· Develop and implement strategies for managing power conversion systems across their lifecycle, including spare parts planning, repowering analyses, and monitoring capabilities.

· Review and validate inverter and BESS firmware, controls logic, and operating parameters to ensure proper system performance and grid compliance.

· Support analysis of inverter and BESS interactions with plant-level controls and grid events to improve system response and stability.

· Identify and evaluate key failure modes and develop mitigation strategies to reduce recurrence and fleet-wide risk.

· Support long-term planning for major component replacements and fleet upgrades.

· Drive reliability improvements through PM optimization, failure trend analysis, and standardization of best practices.

· Support development of condition-based maintenance approaches.

· Provide operational insight to Delivery teams to inform equipment selection and specifications.

· Support commissioning review and project turnover into operations.

· Identify and communicate design or operational deficiencies.

· Collaborate closely with Asset Management, O&M, Performance Engineering, and Compliance teams to improve fleet performance.

Qualifications:

Education

· Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical Engineering preferred)

Experience

· 7+ years working with power conversion systems (solar inverters and/or BESS preferred).

· Strong field experience troubleshooting inverter and/or BESS systems.

· Experience working with vendors and cross-functional teams to resolve technical issues.

· Utility-scale solar, storage, or similar industrial power experience preferred.

Skills

· Strong understanding of inverter technologies, BESS systems, and AC power systems.

· Proven ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues.

· Experience with root cause analysis and reliability practices.

· Strong communication skills and ability to influence outcomes across teams.

What We’re Looking For

· A field-proven engineer who can operate at both site and fleet level.

· Someone who can connect on-site issues to broader system impacts.

· Comfortable owning complex problems and driving them to resolution.

Job Description

Position: Solar Maintenance Technician II – Field Operations

Location: On-site, primarily in the Forrest City, Arkansas region.

Overview: This position is responsible for the performance of corrective and preventative maintenance tasks within a defined set of facilities. These tasks include the inspection, troubleshooting, diagnosis, and remedy of issues impacting the production of the solar PV facility. This includes repair and/or replacement of electrical and mechanical components and subcomponents such as contactors, breakers, motors, bearings, PV modules, PLCs, transformers, etc. This position may also act as a safety second and assist more senior technicians as needed.

The ideal candidate is a self-starter with a strong mechanical inclination and verifiable experience performing in the electrical trade, electrical or multicraft maintenance, or solar operations and maintenance. Experience performing maintenance tasks on DC, AC, and MV systems, communications equipment, and mechanical systems will translate well to this position.

No direct solar PV experience is required.

Main Responsibilities:

  • Perform scheduled preventive maintenance tasks at each facility, including the full PV system, UPS, SCADA, substation, and MV/HV/OHE systems.
  • Perform corrective maintenance tasks, both scheduled and unscheduled, at each facility, including the full PV system, UPS, SCADA, substation, and MV/HV/OHE systems.
  • Respond to directives for emergency dispatches for critical systems as directed.
  • Log all work performed via the Silicon Ranch CMMS platform.
  • Perform electrical testing using IV Curve Tracers, Power Quality Meters, Insulation Resistance Testers, Multimeters, and other testing equipment as needed.
  • Assist management with field investigations to support predictive analytics, root cause analysis, and serial defect reports.
  • Provide site access to third party contractors and as directed.
  • Assist with other site tasks, including land management, module washing, and vegetation management as directed.
  • Attend internal and external training sessions as directed.
  • Must be able to communicate effectively, collaboratively and responsibly with team members and management.
  • Must be able to work alone as a self-starter and work within a team driving towards a common goal.
  • Must be able to stand for long periods of time.
  • Must be able to work outside in most weather conditions.
  • Must be able to lift 50 pounds.

Qualifications:

  • Intermediate skills with computers and electronic equipment required
  • Intermediate skills with Microsoft Office and Adobe Acrobat required
  • Working knowledge of NEC, NFPA70E, and OSHA standards
  • Valid Driver’s License Required
  • OSHA 30 (must be obtained within 4 weeks of employment)
  • CPR/BLS (must be obtained within 4 weeks of employment)
  • State electrical license or NABCEP certification desired
  • Ability to perform localized travel of up to 2 hours each way. Note: The first hour and Last hour of daily driving/travel is not paid. It is considered normal commute time.

Education:

  • High School Diploma or GED

Experience:

  • 3+ years of experience in the electrical trade, electrical maintenance, multicraft maintenance, or the completion of a recognized apprenticeship program required.
  • Solar installation, commissioning, or operations and maintenance experience highly desired.
  • Experience with MV/HV systems, IT systems, inverters, T&D systems, substations, or other specialized electrical systems desired.
